newsitem.title: INDIA: Crisil downgrades Indian Atul debentures.
newsitem.headline: Crisil downgrades Indian Atul debentures.

text.p: The Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) said on Tuesday it downgraded chemicals firm Atul Ltd's outstanding debentures to "AA-" from the earlier "AA" rating.
CRISIL also assigned an AA- rating to Atul's proposed 300 million rupee non-convertible debenture issue, it said in a statement.

"Atul's performance in its dyestuffs business during 1995/96 has been affected by a downturn in the textiles industry, leading to a fall in average sales realisations, increase in debtors' level and sluggish growth in demand," CRISIL said.

But the company enjoyed considerable benefits because of its backward integration, thereby reducing its vulnerability, it said. CRISIL said Atul was now implementing expansion projects in dye intermediates and putting up a captive power plant.
"This is expected to help the company save on power costs and focus on products with higher contribution margin," it said.
